To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

anisotropic effects are found to play a minor role in the quenching process of Fe(Se<sub>x</sub> Te<sub>1-x</sub>) superconducting thin film, and that this behavior is in agreement with a model that describes the quenching as an avalanche-like event.

the quenching and critical currents in Fe(Se) thin films grown by pulsed laser deposition on a CaF2 substrate are both strongly affected by flux pinning and that the quench current is even less sensitive than critical current to angular variations.

the quenching currents in Fe(Se<sub>x</sub>Te<sub>1-x</sub>) thin films are less sensitive to anisotropy than critical currents, and the anisotropy is not related with the pinning strength of the films.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the anisotropy of the quench current of Fe(Se,T)<sub>x</sub> films grown by molecular beam epitaxy on CaF<sub>x</sub>.
the anisotropy of the quench current in iron-based superconducting thin-films and its dependence on the magnetic flux pinning.
the study of the quench current in Fe(Chalcogenides) thin films as a function of magnetic field orientation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anisotropy of the critical current is not the only parameter that determines the anisotropies of the quench current.
the quenching process is less affected by flux pinning than the critical current, which is a consequence of the different mechanisms that determine the two current values.
the anisotropy of Fe(Se<sub>1-x</sub> Te<sub>x</sub>) thin films is not a relevant factor in the observed differences between <italic>I< /sub>c </italic> and I* behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quenching behavior is more robust than the critical current behavior with respect to anisotropy, which is in agreement with the results of other superconducting materials.

the anisotropic properties in the Fe(Se, Te) films are not strong enough to affect the quenching process, thus the <italic>I</sup>*<italic> value is mainly determined by the intrinsic properties of the superconducting material.
, in the case of the quench current, the pinning strength is not affected by the anisotropic properties of the material.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in spite of the strong anisotropic effects on the critical current of Fe(Se) superconducting films, the anisotropy on the quenching currents is weak, and it can be considered as a material property, which can be used to design superconducting devices.
, in Fe(Se,T) thin films, the angular dependence of the quench current is not a strong function of the magnetic field orientation and is not significantly different from the critical current.

, for a given applied magnetic field orientation, the quench event occurs when the current is close to the maximum critical current, regardless of whether the latter is higher or lower than the former.
